newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles school board floats $2.4 bln bond plan.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles school board floats $2.4 bln bond plan.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Board of Education voted to place a $2.4 billion school bond measure on the April 8, 1997 ballot following its defeat in November, school officials said.
The board was unanimous in its support for the measure, which failed in the November election by a narrow margin, officials said.
If approved in April, the bonds would provide funds for the Los Angeles City Unified School District, primarily to improve school facilities.
Voters must approve the issue with a two-thirds majority.
